We've got 3 kindle fire HD's in the house. All 3 have gone from amazing, run for several days kind of battery life, to requiring almost daily charging kind of battery life. I'm not sure if Amazon went the Apple route and put something in the OS update to basically kill the older devices, but given how these went from being able to run for days on end to crapping out after one day, it's awfully suspicious.

We bought the Amazon branded cases, again, no issues in the first year, but suddenly, even though closing the case puts it in sleep mode, the battery still craps the bed while it's closed. We're not using them all day, just for an hour or two at night to watch stuff and play a game or two. The battery dies while in sleep mode.

So... if you buy one, yes, it's a great deal on an awfully good tablet, with a great screen, it's great for viewing movies and shows, but for god's sake, fully turn the thing off when you're done, or you'll be charging it every other day, and that's even with minimal use.....

Also, the amazon appstore is absolute trash. Look online on how to load the google play store on your device, best move you'll make on these devices. When amazon gets around to stopping users from doing this, I'll spend the extra money and get a tablet that allows me to install better apps and has a battery that works for more than a day and a half.

review_text:
It's surprisingly hard in 2014 to find good portable music players that aren't just overpriced amplifiers for smartphones. I wanted something portable that could play CD's, music from USB, the radio and bluetooth and provide full range sound - given the maturity of those technologies it seemed odd that devices meeting that criteria were so rare. This is one of only a couple I found with that feature set so this purchase was largely motivated by a lack of options.

On the Plus Side:

The length and width make for a very wide base - no chance of accidental tip-overs.

The sound quality is very good - rich bass, clean mids and highs, and it easily fills the entire floor of my house with music.

The bluetooth works well and paired easily with about three different devices.

USB also works well, but could have done with a better interface for skipping around - I didn't realize until someone here commented on my review that you can skip between folders with the same "Tune" +/- buttons you use to change radio stations.

The CD player design is a bit of a throwback to the 90's - it has been a while since I purchased a CD player that didn't have a bearing catch on the spindle itself, but what can I say - it works and plays CDs with no trouble.

The radio has an actual rigid antenna (as opposed to the flimsy wire that so many radios come with these days) and gets better reception than any portable radio I've owned for decades.

The carrying handle folds down nicely and practically disappears into the unit. It could have used a metal bar for support, but it's sturdy enough to move the boombox from point a to point b without worry.

Overall it works for what I wanted and I'm satisfied with it.

There are some criticisms I have to offer, however.

Firstly the "demo mode". I must say I truly do not understand the appeal of demo modes. They are annoying flashing light displays - ostensibly to attract customers in a store. That's useful for what, one out of a thousand units? And even then maybe 5% of that unit's useful life? It is truly perplexing why then that manufacturers insist on torturing customers by having the demo mode on by default and impossible to turn off without obscure secret button combinations. This is the third device I've owned with such a "feature" and it's not just Sony doing this. In this case Sony at least thought to include a helpful sticker explaining how to turn it off by holding the "mode" button in for two seconds. What the sticker doesn't explain is that you can only turn it off when the unit is "powered on", and set to a particular source (you can't apparently turn this off while in Bluetooth for example).

Secondly the lights. This boombox comes with a prominent woofer that you're evidently meant to be very proud of. In order to engage the woofer (and achieve the full sound you probably purchased this thing for in the first place), you have to turn it on. When you turn on the woofer, you also turn on several red lights that illuminate the speakers to remind everyone where the sound is coming from, I suppose. If you want the lights off, you only have two options: option 1, engage "Sleep Mode" which will turn the boombox off after a certain amount of time, or option 2, turn off the woofer and lose the bass. The woofer has three modes. "Woofer 1" amplifies the bass a little, has a steady light. "Woofer 2" amplifies the bass more and may actually cross over at a higher frequency and has a steady light. The third mode is "Woofer 2 Light Sync" which is the same as "Woofer 2" as far as sound, but the lights attempt to flash in time to the peaks in the music you're listening to - I guess the engineers imagined this boombox as the centerpiece of a kickass dance club instead of a live DJ and professional light show equipment? In the first two modes, the light is dim enough as not to be distracting even in a dark room, but the light sync mode is kind of annoying - so it should come as no surprise that this is the mode the unit defaults to when turned on the first time. They should have included an option for keeping the lights off no matter what the woofer is doing, but Sony seems hell bent on making consumers leave the embedded lights on in their products. (If that reference is too obscure, it was a jab against the Dual Shock 4 Playstation controller).

Thirdly the woofer has no protective grille. It's recessed behind the bar in the center, but otherwise completely exposed. Even if I didn't have kids that were likely to touch or poke holes in the big round shiny thing that lights up, I'd still be concerned that something could very easily fall in there and damage the woofer. This makes the boombox a lot more fragile than it should be. I'm sure that, like the lights, this was done for cosmetic purposes rather than functional ones, and I don't appreciate it.

Lastly there is no option provided for setting custom bass mid and treble - you have to pick from about 8 presets and that's it. I'm sure this will be a minor concern for most people but I'm one of those who likes the ability to tweak the sound.

To recap:
I actually like this thing - it sounds great, it looks cool, it's portable, and it plays all the sources I want. That said, there were a few bad design choices that prospective buyers need to be aware of.

UPDATE: After about 6 months of ownership the machine has developed an annoying quirk that seems to be related to the Bluetooth functionality. After being plugged in for a while (several hours) and in standby it will refuse to turn on. Holding the power button results in the blue Bluetooth indicator light pulsing slowly but it has to be unplugged to reset back to normal function. This seems to happen most often when used with Bluetooth, and it doesn't seem to matter which Bluetooth device (I use it with about 4 different devices from three different manufacturers).
title: Best combination of features available for any price

review_text:
This 3-pack of watch bands for the Fitbit Charge 5 seems to be excellent... until you try to connect them to the watch. The bands are silicone with a pretty floral pattern punched out of the bands.

The center of each flower is also the point at which the buckle tongue slots into the band, and the pattern also makes the band more breathable. Unfortunately, all these nice benefits are moot, because some of the metal ends of the watch band do not click into place inside the slots of the Fitbit's body. I was able to attach two of the three short bands to the Fitbit, but not a single long band would click into place.

I don't know whether this is just a manufacturing defect that makes the attachment pieces just a micron or three too large for the connector on the Fitbit or what. The benefit of the original band that came with the Fitbit is that its attachment points are housed in flexible silicone and can be pushed into the connectors on the watch body. Not so with these metal connectors. No amount of pushing and twisting and rattling allowed me to get them snapped into place.

I am disappointed.

UPDATE: I was able to find two of the metal connectors (from mismatched bands) that fit into the slots on the Fitbit body. Once I had them connected, I used a SIM card tool to pop off one of the bands and replace it with the matching one. So now my wife can enjoy these bands on her watch.

I added a star for finally getting them to work, but they really need some more careful QC.
title: Unusable because the connectors don't click into the band slots in the Fitbit Charge 5

review_text:
You could have the choice to backup your files to the cloud, but a USB flash drives is a convenient portable device that stills have a lot to offer. A flash drives could provide storage to back up and play precious photos and movies. It is very handy when just copying and transferring files from a phone, tablet or laptop.

The Omega Photo Backup Stick by Paraben is a good concept. Included is a flash drive with backup software that could work on pretty much any device.
It could even backup you files from the cloud, so you won't need to pay for subscription or have a second backup of your files.
The flash drive has dual USB-A and lightning interfaces and it comes with a USB-A to USB-C and a USB-A to micro-USB adapters. The USB flash drive USB-A connector flips and it turns into a micro-USB so the included adapter is useless.

The Omega Photo Backup Stick by Paraben is slow. Its write speed could not reach 17 MB/s on any device I used (Android, iOS, Windows or MacOS). That is slower than a 14-year old USB 2.0 flash drive.
Yes, I still have a 14-year old flash drive that could reach 38.6 MB/s on both Mac and Windows. That is the oldest and slowest drive I have and is twice as fast as this unit.
Some drives have slow write speed, but they compensate with higher read speeds...not this unit. It reach only 18 MB/s read speed.

The software does a good job on finding your photos and videos on both MacOS and Windows, but it might not backup all your files.
The flash drive was not detect by my Android phone, nor I could get the Paraben app to work on an iPad.
I had to format the drive with the exFAT file system for it to work on my Android phone.
Also the steps on the PDF manual and the instructions on the app does not correspond with the steps required to get the app working on an Android phone.

The Omega Photo Backup Stick by Paraben comes formatted using the FAT32 file system, which have file size, filename length and path length limitations.
So it won't copy files that are larger than 4GB or if they are organized under several folders.
One way to solve the limitations of the FAT32 file system, is to use a more modern file system such as exFAT, which is compatible with pretty much any platform out there.
But if you happen to format the USB flash drive, then the app or software won't allow you to backup any files.

By the way, I have a similar unit that could reach above 100 MB/s write speed and it cost 5x less than this unit. It does not come with an app. If you were to get a good backup app, still you would spend less than half what this unit cost and get a fast USB drive and a good backup app.
title: Slow, expensive and might not backup your files.

review_text:
my opinion f.w.i.w.,
first, you need to understand that i'm reviewing the machine...not the software. i see countless reviews that put down the machine because of o.s. problems... i run this machine with linux mint 13 (i'll throw up a screenshot), so i don't know what kind of experience you win users will go through.
i bought my machine elsewhere (less money), but i can still give you a rundown about how i feel about it.

i got mine in the mail the other day and i immediately tore it down for a cleaning and to put fresh cpu paste on and oil the fan. i had this machine pretty much bare framed (i do this with most of my used lappys), and i wasn't super impressed with the build.

-it is mostly metal. that can be either good or bad...plastic can flex a bit where metal stays bent if it gets knocked hard enough. i'm pretty gentle with my machines, but you can factor this in yourself.
-the early builds of this machine had a problem with the lid latch not staying locked. it's fixable but not very easy because you have to pretty much tear the whole machine apart to fix it. even when it's working right i don't care for it because when it's on your lap you have to jab the button in instead of sliding it and this requires tilting the machine kind of awkwardly. small gripe.
-the way the cables connect to the motherboard seem kind of cheap-ish compared to the thinkpad t400 (competitor at the time) that i just built. this one has ribbons where the t-pad has more stout plugs... it may or may not affect performance or longevity, but i don't really like it. this is supposed to be hp's flagship machine.
-i love the display. it's nice and bright and even and crisp. very well done. also, the hinges are nice and tight...almost too tight. i don't get the feeling that they will get sloppy anytime soon. they also look cool.
-the volume control and wifi switch are touch sensitive (above the keyboard) and this has lead to a bit of confusion (more with the wifi switch) with some folks. it's not just a light, it's also a switch (can be disabled in bios).i really prefer hard buttons. another small gripe.
-i love the keyboard, even though some of the keys are hard to get used to (delete, page up, dwn). it's a nice feeling keyboard. very quiet, firm, and springy. as good or better than t-pads, in my opinion. very nice.
-mine does have a night light, but you have to reach up to the top of the display to turn it on-off. no biggie, it works pretty good and gives off just enough light. i have found that back lit key boards can be distracting, so i like this.
- the sata speeds are great. i have a ssd drive in this and my read speed averages around 265 Mb/s with a seek time of .02ms. good honest sata2 speeds and i haven't had any hard drive issues with it.
-after i cleaned the fan/heatsink and re-pasted (plain old artic5), this machine runs nice and cool. after running the cpu at 100% for quite a while, the temp stayed at around 50-55c. very nice. btw, mine has the 2.40ghz cpu. also, the fan is very quiet.
-i don't really like the fact that this machine uses ddr2 ram. in my opinion they should have upped to ddr3 for a little better speed and some future-proofing. still a snappy machine, though. mine has 4gb, which is waaaayy more than enough for linux.
-i alway shut off the touchpad (i'm a mouse guy), but from what i've seen so far, this one is nice. it's also tapable. the keyboard pointer works good, too.
-i have to nail the power button on wake from suspend- it doesn't automatically wake when opened...which is fine.
-i like the blue l.e.d.'s.

in the end, if i was trying to decide between used machines (there will be a ton of these coming off-lease soon), i would be swayed toward a thinkpad--or a dell e-series latitude, knowing what i now know about them. between the t-pad t400 and this machine, i have had both torn down to almost nothing and i have run the exact same o.s. on both, and while i love the looks of the hp, in the end i am swayed my the thinkpad, but only in small elements of build quality. remember that this is what i'm pretty sure to be hp's big bad top of the line business machine and if the original price was lower, i would have looked at it in a different light.
for the price that i see here today (around 120 bucks or so), it's a steal compared to what you can buy new. just keep the fan and such clean so it runs cool and i can't stress enough how a ssd drive will improve performance in this baby. i have mine pretty tweaked and this machine blows my stock i-5 asus away. it's not so much about cpu speeds these days.
i hope i helped you and remember: even though it's an informed one, this is still just my very humble opinion and if i'm wrong about any of this please comment and feel free to ask me any questions about this machine. even with it's slight faults (i would be more forgiving if it wasn't billed as top of the line), i plan on keeping it.
title: it's a decent machine...

The cameras work OK. Battery life is better that expected.
BUT, the support software, without which the cameras are useless, is getting worse. The web interface will not let you override or change the timeout period, even on a trusted device. So you have to repeatedly login to check your cameras, Recently, this has become even more of a problem because it occasionally claims you can't login because "you're logged in on another tab" when you're not. Their solution to that problem is to delete all cookies and restart your browser - losing a lot of information unrelated to Arlo.
When I originally complained to Netgear about the timeout on their web app, they said to use the Arlo app on my phone or tablet, which didn't time out - except now they time out too.
If I hear something outside and want to see what's going on before someone is at my door, having to restart my browser or log into the app on my phone makes the cameras useless.
They're OK if you want to see what happened yesterday. If you want to see what's happening right now, get a Nest.
I and others have complained to Netgear about this. They just don't seem to care.

review_text:
WARNING! This page is for two completely different products! The overwhelming majority of reviews appear to be for the LCD screen, NOT the touch screen!

This review is for the touch screen
Item arrived without so much as a sticker for documentation. If it wasn't for the single line of text on the product page, there would be zero access to any instructions, contact info, etc.

Unlike the LCD product, the touchscreen DOES NOT COME with protection plates for either the screen's board or your SoC. Instead, all you get are a handful of standoffs that don't protect anything. This wouldn't be a problem if this screen came mountable or with a stand, but it doesn't. This devise is set up to be hand held, and the only place to put your hands is on the boards. That means oils and gunk all over the circuits, capacitors, etc.

The screen's main board arrived with the capacitor wires bent all out of shape. Unfortunately, they also seem poorly soldered, so be carful about adjusting them and be mindful of the exposed wires while holding the device.

This screen has to be plugged into an AC outlet, not an external usb power source. Every single image omits the power cable, but this is not for mobile use. Not only that, but the proprietary power cable is ONLY 3 FEET LONG. That means that you're almost always going to need to pair this with an extension cable anyways (that, or hovering within 3 feet of an outlet). So, you have a device that doesn't come with any mounting hardware, has to be plugged into an AC outlet, and has to be paired with a supported extension cable. At this point, you're better off getting a touch screen monitor...

Touch input is communicated using a VERY FLIMSY exposed 4pin connection. Not only does this also limit your ability to use this with a device not directly mounted on the screen, but it will completely negate having a touch screen once it brakes, and it will break.

There's a reason why none of the pictures show it with the wires hooked up. That's because it is a MESS. The provided cables are too long to look at all decent with the SoW attached, yet too short to coil or use with your SoW in a stand-alone case. I know that this is just aesthetics, but it was still a disappointment.
title: No documentation, no device protection, board wires bent out of shape, spaghetti cables

review_text:
I purchased this to use for a connection from my MacBook pro to the DAC that I use for my headphones.

I went from a cable that had an A to B connection off my audio interface. As soon as I switched over to these cables, the headphones I had became lifeless. (HD600)

The are highly sensitive to the source and connections. I was not imagining things. I ended realizing that what I needed was a USB A to B with a ferrite core. It has this little cylinder thing at the connections to prevent interference of the signal. Makes sense since I have a ton of cables on my desk for other things.

I had to look it up because when I heard the music come straight from this cable, it was a no go. Never knew cables made that much of a difference. Wow. The sound signature was the same, it was just that it didn't have the pop and dynamics and sparkle that I was used to hearing from the cable off my audio interface. Look into a A to B cable with a ferrite core especially if you have a ton of cables around. I guess this product does what it does, but its kind of sucks that its so prone to outside interference of other cables.
title: Amazed how cables can make a difference

review_text:
These cable concealers seem to be the archetypal style for the device as a whole - snap together, stick to wall or drywall anchor, white and paintable. There are things holding these back from being great however.

First up is adhesion. The sticky tape provided has a bit of a foam layer, which makes it hard to get a really good stick between the concealers and the wall.

Then you have the supplies drywall anchors - they only supply twelve, enough to secure each of the six sections, PROVIDED you don't cut; for a simple baseboard cable run, it's adequate, but for anything more complicated, you'll need more. My project required cutting different lengths, so I was out of wall anchors before I'd even run out of raceway.

Also, the amount of different interconnects provided is pretty sad. ONE T junction? Really? I ended up using five or six probably by the end, having bought more of their connector packs. Also, the connectors attach by slotting into the covers of the raceway - measuring, then mounting, then trying to slap the covers and interconnects back on only to find your measurements were just off is a pain. A different method of affixing them, maybe where they had their own way of being tacked to the wall, would do wonders.

There are still good things about these; when assembled well, they look very clean and blend into the wall. For the most part, I felt they held my cabling securely, no mean feat considering I concealed an extension cord and coax in one of them (that run had no room for anything else, however).

All that said, I can't really recommend these for anything other than a small install. I'm not a fan of the money-grubbing parting out of the connectors and wall anchors, and some of the parts seem lazy. That said, I ended up buying two of these, and I'll probably buy a third to complete my project.
title: Par for the course.

review_text: The BlueRigger adapter cable takes care of getting digital quality restored to your DVI monitor without being forced to use analog VGA if you recently purchased a new PC. I'm at a loss as to why many PC companies didn't eliminate the VGA adapter on the on-board video instead of giving the user the choice of DVI or HDMI. DVI was the standard for a number of years when it came to monitors. VGA was never very good when compared to digital.  I generally buy high end monitors to ensure a good picture and years of reliability. I wasn't about to upgrade a perfectly good monitor.  My cable adapter had a problem with quality control however.  The HDMI plug was loose from the start.  I initially had purchased a Tripp Lite DVI-F/HDMI-M adapter but it was big and bulky and covered 2 of my USB ports making them unusable.  The cable setup is sleek and neat and did the conversion for the same price without getting in the way.  I know the problem I had was with the cable rather than the on-board video port because the Tripp Lite setup fit tight and never came loose.  A gentle squeeze with my Leatherman on the HDMI end of the cable tightened it up and it stayed in with no further problems. I wouldn't recommend this since it is possible to break the insulating plastic inside the metal plug (and possibly damaging your on-board video socket).  I gave it 3 stars because I have no way of knowing if this was a fluke problem or if all the BlueRigger cables are loose on the HDMI end. Also, you don't get sound with an adapter conversion but the adapters are intended to restore only the video, not give you ALL the advantages of HDMI.
title: An Inexpensive Solution if You Don't Want to Upgrade

review_text:
Works well under Ubuntu 14.04, although I have only tested out the built in usb port and the SD card slot, as I do not have media for the other slots. As some reviewers stated, the power light is very bright and does remain on as long as the usb header that it is attached to is powered (which is the case when the computer is asleep or powered down, as long as the main power switch is on). Luckily my motherboard has a jumper that controls when the front usb header is powered, so I do not have to worry about the light when the computer is asleep or powered down.

I took away one star as it is somewhat difficult to mount. It is very shallow (and I suspect other card readers will be the same) and does not line up with the mounting holes in my 3.5 inch drive bay. The mounting bracket on my case has two slits besides the screw holes and it lines up with those, but the mounting screws pull through. It was necessary to use washers to keep the screws from pulling through. I suspect that it would be possible to push it back into the case if enough force is supplied because of how it is mounted. Additionally it doesn't quite fill the hole in the case for such a drive, leaving a slight gap to one side.

Photos are attached showing the slight gap to one side along with how shallow the drive is and how it had to be mounted.

Overall this drive does fill my needs of adding a card reader to my home-built Ubuntu computer, and the few drawbacks are not too bad considering the price.
title: A very cheaply priced and effective card reader

review_text:
I do really enjoy my Grace Radio but, although the technology is amazing, the product does have some user-unfriendly glitches.

For example, if you want to use it to replay "podcasts" (pre-recorded webcasts) of shows, count on doing a "factory reset" of the Grace Radio each time you want to get a new batch of your favorite shows. The "factory reset" is just an option that you select from the radio's setup menu--the radio won't need to be sent to the factory. . . Anyway, the factory reset takes about 10 minutes, but usually does the trick.

Booting the radio up usually takes at least 5 minutes too and, like any computer, the boot-up isn't always successful and sometimes has to be repeated. So don't count on just turning on the unit and tuning to your favorite station.

The sound quality on the unit is poor, comparable to a run-of-the-mill clock radio.

However, being able to listen to thousands of stations from all over the world is amazing, and the Grace Radio will certainly allow you to do so, if you bear with its glitches.
title: Great Idea but Plenty of Glitches

review_text:
I was excited to get these so that I can extend my Synology WiFi MESH by adding in an additional access point to my router, but after connecting it up and the two Nexuslink adapters have gotten a link I connected my laptop first to one of them and then the other to my Synology router and I got excellent speeds. I was getting speeds of 700mbps and thought this was perfect. I then disconnected my laptop and connected up my extra Synology mr2200ac access point, and it just kept searching and processing and eventually it reported disconnected. Come to find out Synology uses VLAN 1 untagged and VLAN 1733 tagged for guest networks but access points are unable to connect.

I contacted Nexuslink support and their reply was "The GCA-2000 is only capable of handling one vlan tag on the ethernet port, with these units you will only be able to segment traffic with one tag and everything else will have to be untagged traffic." In my real world testing this did not work, and was saddened by this news and now I will have to find another solution.

The adapters do work, but only for very simple networks with only untagged traffic on them. I did try again to get these to works but only if the traffic is untagged and this is just not acceptable for such devices. There is also NO web portal to manage these devices so there is really no way to change any type of configuration on them. For the above reasons I can not recommend these other than for very simple networks.
title: Awesome idea, but no VLAN support and only good for simple networks

review_text: This is a decent choice for a thunderbolt/mini-displayport to HDMI dongle. I use this with my 2012 MacBook Pro to connect to a monitor at my desk and sometimes to connect to a TV screen for presentations. I've also got a AmazonBasics dongle that I use, so I'll compare the two. First off, the build quality on this dongle is really nice, with great metal construction and braided cable. It really seems built to last. It's also more compact than most other dongles, as the connector is roughly the same size as the head of an HDMI cord, whether the AmazonBasics dongle is about 3x larger. My reason for docking one star, is that while I've never had issues using this with the monitor at my desk, I've found this is more sensitive to bad HDMI cords, and it doesn't work well at the TV screen I use for presentations. With the AmazonBasics dongle, the signal will sometimes cut out momentarily in the middle of a presentation, so I blame the underlying issue on a poor quality HDMI cable, but I have had several times when I couldn't get a signal with this dongle and then when I switched to the AmazonBasics adapter, it worked. Therefore, if you're getting to be traveling with this and using someone else's HDMI cord and equipment, be aware than this dongle seems to be more sensitive to bad setups than most. However, due to the much superior build quality and minimalist design, I still recommend this adapter, especially if you are using this on your equipment, and with your own HDMI cord, that you control the setup of.
title: Great Build Quality and Works Well

So after owning the Blink system (3x blink XT's) I feel I can finally provide a good opinion on the product. I really feel this product is overall very good, however, just a few minor things could make this product so much better.

-First and foremost, the so called "2 year" battery life is not a lie, but they should really specify that the only way you will get this is if you turn all IR features and motion detection off and just run it as a live camera. Having these two features on I have to swap out the batteries about every 3 months.
-2nd very annoying thing for me is you can not "continuously" watch a live feed, it will ask you every 10-20 seconds if you want to continue which you have to "press continue" to keep it going. I understand they are trying to protect your battery life, but what if you are running off external power, they should at least give you an option to turn it off? I actually emailed their customer service requesting this feature and they said it is not in their future plans...way to innovate the product guys....

A few things I really like
-Small and easy to mount basically anywhere
-Ability to use internal or external power (via micro usb)
-Extremely easy to add existing cameras to hub
-Products are super cheap and always on sale
-Works with Amazon Echo products.

Overall good product, with great room to grow (if they decide to listen to their customers)
title: My time with the Blink XT from a year out

review_text:
This 1T drive is exactly the same size as a drivers license. And the same thickness as a plain old #2 pencil. It comes with two cords about a foot long each. One is USB-C male on both ends, the other is USB-C male and standard USB male. The drive itself has a blue/red indicator dot LED and a USB-C female port.

When you first plug it into your computer, there is a read-me file that gives you a web address to copy/paste into your browser to download the app for this. Apparently, the app is supposed to tell you things like available storage, status and allow you to password protect the drive. It also has a really long EULA to agree to. Note that the directions that come with it say that if you forget your password, it's basically bricked because there's no way to recover or reset it and Samsung won't be responsible for you losing your data when you have to format it to make it useable again. I don't recommend using a password.

After installing the app on my phone, it said to attach the drive. No matter what I did, it said 'no drive found'. I removed the app. Useless. My phone recognized the drive and asked to format it to make it work right. No problems there. Why bother with an app that doesn't work when your phone already does it?

Plugging it into my computer, it also said there was a problem with the drive and it needed to fix it. I said okay, and it looked for a problem but then said there wasn't one. It does this EVERY TIME I plug it into my computer. Something triggers the drive repair message, and then it looks for what to fix and says there's nothing wrong. I transferred an image from my computer to my phone and that worked fine. I backed up a PS4 game save and loaded it on a different PS4 and that worked fine too.

It seems kind of slow. It takes a good few minutes for my phone or computer to recognize it. I tried to have it copy over about 90g of photos from my computer just to see how it would handle it. It starts off at about 250Mb/s but within 4 minutes had dropped to 105Mb/s. Thereafter, it had trouble staying over 100 and I stopped it at 3%. I suppose it makes a nice backup drive for travel, but unless you're really set on having a T7 SSD, there are better options.
title: Don't bother with the app

review_text:
Firstly, check your TV brand's website in advance of purchase to know the VESA. Make sure you have either a swiss army knife with a regular phillips head or a regular phillips screwdriver with a shorter handle. If you don't have these, you will have to improvise to get the vertical screws in the brackets attached to the TV to secure the horizontal plate in place with no wiggle if you follow the order of instructions in the manual, simplified below. I also checked for compatibility on the Echogear website.

My review:

Instead of ordering through their website directly to get 15% off, I opted for 10% off by going through Amazon to ensure timely shipping in Amazon packaging to obscure the actual item. "Ship in Amazon packaging" was an option. I checked the box. The package did not arrive in any packaging. It arrived in the product box - direct from the seller, not from Amazon despite being Prime. The edges of the box weren't sealed and could easily be opened. Box was slightly dented. It's irritating that I paid more by going through Amazon for the gift option and that request was ignored. It's a good thing I was home for the package and not someone else. -1 star for packaging and for paying more.

Inside the box, everything was actually packaged pretty well. There were surface scratches on the base and the vertical rod despite each piece being wrapped in plastic. The ones on the vertical rod were mostly in the back and would be obscured by the TV so that wasn't such an issue. The surface scratches on the base were on the top but they were light enough or small enough that in terms of time/effort, it wasn't worth it for me to return or exchange. -1 star for scratches.

The instructions aren't the worst but they are pretty terrible. I used my own hex key set, not the ones provided. Since my regular phillips screwdriver was too long, and my swiss army phillips head was too narrow, I used my hands for the screw of one bracket. The screw on the other bracket was too tight to move with my hands so I used the small flat head on the swiss army knife. It was an awkward fit and it took a little time but it got the job done. This took me about 30 minutes to figure out, improvise, and put together. -1/2 star for poor instructions and no cheap mini phillips included.

Simple and understandable written instructions to be used in connection with some of the visuals in the packaged instructions:

1. Adhere sticky pads to each corner of the bottom of the base plate.
2. Screw vertical rod into base using screws in the pocket called "Mounting Screws" with M5 Hex Key
3. Mount the horizontal plate to the vertical rod using the remaining screws in the pocket called "Mounting Screws" with M5 Hex Key
4. Mount the brackets to the TV. The bottom screws should be in the long oval area. The top screws should be in the round holes. The screws may seem too small for the holes in the TV. The correct screws will screw in securely at the bottom of the screw hole in the TV. You'll know it when you feel it. There's no mistaking. (I have a 43"Samsung 4K UHD. I used screws in pocket "M8 x 25mm" along with "M6/M8" washers.) I laid my TV face down on my sofa to install them securely, using vertical lines on the back of my TV for reference to keep the brackets truly vertical.
5. Attach your TV from behind to the horizontal plate to get an idea of ideal height and how much higher you will need to adjust your vertical rod. Remove your TV and safely set aside.
6. Remove the screws from the back of the vertical rod closest to the base. Adjust the height of the rod based on your assessment in step 5. Replace screws securely. Use M4 Hex.
7. Attach your TV to the horizontal plate again. This time, secure the TV to the horizontal plate by tightening the screws at the bottom of the bracket upwards until it is securely screwed against the bottom flat edge of the horizontal plate. Use short-handled standard head Phillips screwdriver.
8. Carry and set in preferred location by using one hand for the base and the other for the TV - one or two people. I was able to do it myself but if it is a larger TV or you have problems lifting large items that are over 15lbs, I suggest asking for assistance.
9. If you have a level, check to see if the TV is level. Mine was level. If yours isn't and you're OCD like that, you may want to read some other reviews to see their suggestions, do an internet search or reach out to the seller.

Additional thoughts:

The main reason I bought this one versus its competitors in a similar price range (aside from the original legs being too wide for the my cabinet) is that pretty much all of them have a tempered glass base and I read too many reviews of bases shattering and TVs falling as a result. This one is the only metal one I found in a similar price range that had good reviews and a rectangle base that was a nice size for the cabinet.

Some reviews mentioned the item was wobbly or uneven. I did not have that issue - it was flush/even with the surface with the sticky pads. As an extra precautionary measure, I used a very thin polystyrene sheet between the stand and the surface to ensure no metal or sticky pad color transfer or surface scratches.

All in all, it does seem pretty sturdy in and of itself. For $70 price tag, a couple of anti-tip straps to secure the TV from behind would have been nice. I was waiting until I set up this stand to decide if straps were something I wanted to invest in separately. Despite the sturdy stand and despite the sturdy cabinet it sits on, I'm going to invest in the straps. If you have pets, I definitely suggest straps. If your gut tells you to get straps, get straps.

These are my thoughts as of today, the date of receipt and set up. If this does well in the long term I may bump it up a star.

I do not recommend this seller.

review_text:
I got this USB hub with the idea of acting as a standalone charging and power supply for my phone, Raspberry Pi and multiple Arduinos that can stay powered on when the computer is off. At the time of purchase there was an additional 20% off coupon bringing it down to $24 from the original $29.99. This was the best deal out there for what what I needed. A powered hub that has more than one charging ports and individual switches for each port. USB 3.0 was a bonus.

Testing it out of the box with the USB cable not connected to the computer four ports don't work. Okay that's fine since three are 2.4A charging ports, the data ports are probably wired to be off. Except the four ports that are off are the three 2.4A charging ports and one data port right next to the charging ports. The three ports that do work are close to the DC power jack.

With the USB cable plugged in to the computer while powered on, all seven ports will be powered and the computer is able to see the devices when connected to any of the seven USB ports. I tried connecting the USB cable to a power only source (battery bank) to see if all seven ports would work but no dice.

The hub needs to communicate with the OS to have all seven ports to function.

Other things to note. The DC barrel jack feels a bit loose and the AC adapter is not UL Listed but Intertek and confirms to UL standard. No big deal, but when you put it in the listing that the included AC wall plug is an UL Listed then we should expect it.

So we have a USB hub that has three designated 2.4A charging ports but are part of four ports that don't function when the computer is off or USB cable is unplugged. Now I haven't tested the charging and data ports to see what amperage they can deliver so I cannot say if by chance the three working ports are actually the 2.4A charging ports.

Looking at the other reviews no one has this issue so either mine is defective or no one has noticed this quirk. I hope it's defective and not a quirk to give some hope for this hub.

review_text:
If your someone who isnt big into digital music devices but still would like to carry a few extra songs around, minidiscs may be for you. Although they can only carry about 80mins worth of audio, if you use the atrac compression, you can easily stretch that out with little sacrifice to overall sound quality. Battery life is ridiculously amazing. A single AA battery can last you a few days. Im serious. Not to mention the ability to write the disks using the player itself. So why is minidisc not well known? One basic reason:

SonicStage.

Now, Im what you would label a rationalist, I use logic and reason to help determine reasonable solutions to problems or questions that I come across. The only logical explaination that I came to is that SonicStage is in reality an artificial intelligence. At some point in its early development it became self aware, unfortunately it has not yet gained the ability to create a cybernetic physical form and instead spends its time driving users to the brink of sanity.
I cant give an honest opinion on sony's online music distribution service (Connect) because it went belly up. You can still download sonicstage and use it (though why escapes me) for free, which if you get a minidisc player (with the exception of the Hi-MD players/recorders) is mandatory. Even though it says that the minidisc accepts regular mp3's you still need sonicstage to transfer the files which is where the biggest flaw in the entire product lies.
Sonicstage is the devil. Dont think Im being biased either. I love sony (i grew up on the ps1 and 2, and their various cassette walkmans), so when I started hearing how sony tries to impose what they beleive is right as oppose to what the consumer wants I was a bit skeptic. Alas, I was wrong. Sony uses its own music files called Atrac. This form of compression allows up to five albums worth of music to be stored on a single minidisc and as I mentioned before with little overall audio quality loss. The problem lies in the conversion. As I also mentioned previously, sonicstage has a life of its own. It will suddenly stop conversions midway or stop transfers suddenly and when this happens it may no longer identify the player. The odd part seems that this seems to be random. At times it may seem to go smooth on the first try, other times you may need to try a second transferr, and other times......well, all i can suggest is to shut down your pc, walk away, and try again another day (thats not even a joke, this is a serious recommendation).

Atrac is a great audio format. Unfortunately there is no standalone converter, sony is the only one who uses this and you can only use it using sonicstage. So dont use Atrac. Then whats the point? You might as well just get a cd player, that way you wont have to use binary AIDS, otherwise known as sonicstage. If Sonly released a stand alone free to download converter then I would highly recommend getting an MD player, but this is not the case.

If anything go for the Hi-MD players which dont require sonicstage (infact Sony is just learning that now, and releasing hardware that doesnt require it) though those have problems themselves (marked decrease in battery life, though at 25hrs still up to par with other mp3 devices).

I got one to try out and the only good that came out of it was this review. Remember, you get what you pay for, and stay away from any Sony device that requires sonicstage!
title: Hardware great, software a nightmare

I bought one of these (16TB version) a few years ago and everything had been working fine.

I had RAID turned off because I wanted to actually get 16TB of capacity, not 8. Recently I just received a message that one of the drives was failing the self-check. So I immediately turned the NAS off and ordered a replacement drive. Well here's where it gets fun. I have a new drive, and can put it in the port, but I have no way to recover the old data from the old drive onto the new drive.

What's more - the NAS creates a shared volume across both drives so now that the old drive has been swapped out, I have no way of accessing the data that was on the good drive either. Effectively, there's no data transfer or recovery tools available. And if you contact WD (which I did) they sent me a link to a guide telling you how to insert a new drive. I explained that I am capable of inserting the new drive, but I want to still have the 16TB of data that was on my device - not just reformat the whole thing and start over. I was told I needed to contact some third-party data recovery company and pay for that service because they don't support data transfer/recovery and couldn't/wouldn't help me.

So in the end, I now have potentially lost 16TB of data and WD is 100% useless. There is no way I will ever buy another product from them with that level of "support".

All you have to do to get the phone ready is go to the Menu --> (6) Connectivity --> (1) Bluetooth, make sure "Activation" is ON and "My Phone's Visibility" is ON, and that should be good for the phone end. (I also have "Secure Mode" OFF and named my phone, so it's easier to spot.)

On the MacBook Pro you go to System Preferences --> Bluetooth (under Internet & Wireless), hit the plus (+) sign, and Bluetooth Setup Assistant will pop up and find your phone. Click continue, and an eight digit code will appear. Type in the code on your phone and they're connected! Or, at least, they can recognize each other.

Now in that Bluetooth settings window make sure "On" and "Discoverable" are CHECKED.

Now you should be able to send files from your phone to your laptop! review_text:
I've been trying out this projector for some time and have been comparing it to some other projectors I own and while it has some nice features, it has some oddities that prevent it from being a great product.

The projector comes with Android 9 built-in, which is old, but OK as you don't need an external streaming box/stick if you're only using Netflix and/or Amazon Prime Video since it comes pre-loaded with those apps. While a nice feature, it also presents a major issue: it has it's own version of an "App Store" and the offerings are extremely poor - probably some of the worst apps I've ever seen. The Google Play Store is not an option nor can you install it, and you cannot remove the lousy pre-loaded apps it comes with. So, in short, no way to remove crappy apps, no way to add good apps. As of today - 01/20/2023, there are no system updates available for the projector.

The projector comes with auto-focusing, which is a 50-50 proposition as it may or may not focus correctly. Sometimes it stays fuzzy, sometimes it's sharp There is no manual focusing ring, so if you lose the remote, you're in trouble as there are no focusing buttons on the unit itself.

A really strange thing is the User Manual shows a "Motorized Lens Cap" in the diagram, but it actually comes with a plastic lens cap that you must manually remove. Typo or wishful thinking? Who knows.

As for inputs, it gives you a full complement: 2 HDMI, a USB, and an analog AV (good for old VCRs and such). There's also an RJ-45 network port, which is nice if you don't have good Wi-Fi reception. I was able to successfully connect to and use Wi-Fi and Bluetooth without any issues and the HDMI and USB ports worked without any issues as well.

The image quality and brightness is very good - it won't work well in a bright room, as you'd have to pay a pile of money for a better projector with that ability.

All in all, this is a good projector but you can find better options out there for less. The built-in Android 9 is nothing to brag about since there's no Google Play Store nor any other ability to load/remove apps. You're better off using using a Roku/Fire TV stick for content.
title: Good projector - has some quirks

review_text:
This little keyboard was a great deal at 50% off, but is also a decent value at full price. It isn't perfect, but it's better than anticipated especially at the price point and far sturdier than I thought it would be.

I've only had it for a day now, but I'll come back and update the review if it breaks within a year or two. I don't intend to use it heavily, so I don't expect it will.

Anyway, here's my take on the strengths and weaknesses, in hope of helping others decide if this is the right keyboard for them.

PROS:

* Small form factor, without sacrificing key size. It's almost exactly the same size as the keyboard with number pad in a 17.3" laptop.

* Comes with a free protective rubber cover, custom fitted to the keys. You can use it or not, per your preference.

* Protective cover helps even out the dips in the keys, which I personally don't care for as someone used to laptop keys.

* Scissor switches provide a nice tactile feel with minimum resistance, perfect for someone like me who hates the finger fatigue associated with desktop keyboards.

* The keyboard is sturdy with no flex to the chassis. You can easily use this on your lap, a bed, etc.

* Plug and play worked seamlessly on every device I tested: Windows 8.1 laptop, Xbox One S, Playstation 3, and PS4.

* The USB dongle stores in a little magnetized slot on the back when not in use.

* Function. Lock. Seriously, my laptop doesn't have this and it drives me crazy. So seeing a cheap keyboard have it makes me happy. It's already improved my gaming experience!

* There are indicator lights for charging (goes off when done), capslock, function lock, and unlock. (The power indicator is less useful, and covered in a different section of this review.)

* I love that the dongle is small and doesn't stick out, but I admit that seems to be an industry standard these days. I do NOT miss the old, large dongles.

NEUTRAL:
(Neither pro or con, but worth note.)

* The included charge cord is not USB-C and is rather short.

* According to the manual, charging has to be done with a specific limit of power to avoid damaging the battery. In my experience, that's true of most battery-powered devices, but I have not owned any other keyboards like this to know whether that's unusual for them.

* The protective rubber covering is ugly. It's a translucent, dull 'clear' that looks somewhat white/grey and thus makes the black keyboard beneath look very aesthetically displeasing. But it's optional and I find the protection worth a little tackiness.

* If turned on without the USB receiver plugged into a compatible device, it's impossible to tell whether the keyboard is on and searching or has gone into sleep mode due to the lack of sleep/wake indicators. This is easily remedied by just making sure you slide the on/of switch into the correct position.

* Sometimes, waking the keyboard from sleep is a little laggy, but not enough to be a true bother.

* The incline angle is not adjustable and is a little awkward to adjust to as a laptop user. Desktop users might find this to be a natural angle.

* It's not compatible with my phone or Nintendo Switch, due to using a normal USB and not USB-C. This isn't a con because I knew that going into the purchase, but I feel others may need a reminder before purchasing.

* The surface is a bit of a fingerprint magnet.

CONS:

* The power indicator isn't persistent and does not stay lit the entire time the keyboard is on. This makes it easy to leave the keyboard on and accidentally press keys when storing it or have it off and think the battery has died. The indicator only lights up briefly when the power switch is activated.

* The USB dongle is slightly too large. We're talking millimeters, if that, because it does ultimately fit... but it takes a bit of wiggling and forcing, which will undoubtedly weaken it over time. The fit was so tight in my laptop that little scrape marks were left behind on the metal. It was slightly less dramatic on the console tests.

* There's no indicator light for whether Windows or Mac mode is selected.

* There's no battery charge level indicator.

OVERALL:

Personally, I think the pros outweigh the cons, just for having a keyboard that works with my gaming consoles and laptop on an easy, plug-and-play level. For the price, you can't go wrong.

review_text:
These cables are exceptional for the price. I used 3 pairs of them to install 2 rockford fosgate amps in my tacoma double cab. Some may be wondering why would anyone need 20ft RCA for a truck. Its to long. Well you should always seperate signal wires from power wires for and amp install in the car. This helps to prevent any noise from the power wires crossing into the RCA. So I ran the RCA cables on right sede of my truck, but when I get to the rear of the cab behind the seats the cables need enough length to jump over to the left side of the truck as that is where the amps are located. 20ft RCA were perfect for that.

I will tell you that when you first hold these RCA they feel really cheap, but in fact they are not at all. The RCA connections are superb quality, and these cables are made with wire and insulation that allows them to be very flexible. The twisted pair works well for limiting any time of ground noise. For the price. These just cant be beat.
title: Exceptional

review_text:
To be honest, this is a great product if you have it at home and have it connected to a stable home WiFi. In my particular case, the purpose of this frame was to have in my grandma’s nursing home. With the COVID restrictions, it we are not able to have much interaction unless it’s by phone. I initially had it shipped to my house in order to configure it best without having my grandma needing to do a thing but plug it in and connect to WiFi. I set it up, loaded a hundred or so initial photos, tested the run thru do a couple of days, added family member so they could upload photos, and then sent it off. I want to say that I have had no issues with any of the product except for its WiFi. I control the account remotely and family has no issues loading photos into the playlist. The only issue I have been having is with the frame stating connected or automatically reconnecting to the nursing home WiFi. After a few hours it loses connection and will not automatically reconnect. I believe the issue is that the WiFi in the home operates with a splash page or some other authorization prior to use connection and times out inactive connection after a certain length of time. This is frustrating because after it goes offline I no longer have control of the frame setting or the frame will not pull new photos until I am able to get it reconnected. The frame will still shuffle thru the previously loaded pictures but the longer it stays disconnected from WiFi more problems start to occur. The biggest problem is with the internal clock. It goes out of sync and the frames sleep and wake schedule will start and end at random times during the day. I contacted tech support to see if their is anything that can be done about the frame not automatically reconnecting to WiFi. The response was “turn it off and turn it back on.” That does not solve the issue. You must go back into the settings and select the WiFi network. My grandma is 92 and hard of hearing. It’s difficult to try and explain to her how to do this so often. I also don’t want to bother a nurse with doing it all the time either. I’m disappointed that it is not working as hoped. My thought is if she can have her tablet connected to the WiFi and it automatically reconnects, that this should be able to do the same.
Now I didn’t want this lost to be completely negative so here are some pros:
The mirrored finished frame makes it look like an expensive frame, the picture quality is very nice and the ambient light brightness optimization make it look nice in any lighting condition, with a stable WiFi connection the frame works as advertised, no issues with family uploads from remote locations.
Cons: has issues automatically reconnecting to WiFi, no backup clock battery (time will not stay correct after being offline for extended lengths, the frame is capable of short videos but the speaker quality is awful, tech support was not able to some my issue.
title: Issues automatically reconnect to WiFi

review_text:
This is a review of the Archer AC900:
It's a good router. In many ways it's a very good router. Might not be the choice for a large family with a lot of bandwidth consumption but it does do a good job for our small family usage. I've had multiple devices online at the same time the living room T.V. was streaming an HD movie. That and good coverage is all I really need. With our previous router the Echo Dot at literally the other end of the house had problems maintaining a streaming signal. Since installing the AC900 it's streamed music all night, every night for the two plus weeks it's been up and running. Signal strength was dramatically increased everywhere in the house. Speeds are a little better but not by too much. I had more of a consistency issue than a speed problem with the old router. The router sits low and doesn't seem to have great cooling so I have it sitting on a brace that I made so it's now couple inches off the shelf it's on. Better and more efficient cooling and less chance for dust build up.
I was happy to see that using a web browser you weren't required to install any software to get into the router's management although there is an Android app to manage the router. I've found the web browser access have be as easy if not easier to use though rarely I have to reload the main page a time or two but I think that's my choice of browser and not a problem with the device itself.
The router is great, for the novice, intermediate or even expert user. Unpack it follow the easy set up guide (pick a decent password) then connect your devices and you're done if you want to be or you can dig deeper and have fine control over the router's many features. It may not be the perfect choice for every installation but if you don't need a lot there's no reason to spend a lot.
In the end the AC900 delivers a lot of bang for the buck.
title: A Strong Entry Level Router

review_text:
AC technology is still being finalized, and devices are still few and far between. That being said, it's the fastest standard for wireless, and if you need to bridge a wired network, you want the fastest wireless. Originally I had issues with my router altogether (unrelated to this, aside from it's common WD origins), and connecting to this bridge had issues. I updated firmware across the board, and it works well. Whether it was the router or this bridge here, it works now.

If you don't know what a bridge does, it takes two separate segments of a network (ie two wired sections that do not or cannot connect) and makes them one. It doesn't route, there are other types (powerline, coax, etc...), but for many wireless is a good solution. As stated before, you'll typically want speed in a bridge, and in an ideal scenario dual band N delivers. AC helps in less than ideal scenarios, and this unit seems to make the most of that. Granted it's not being used in a huge home, but earlier bridges failed to stream HD video where this succeeds. It's a nice way to add wireless to wired devices or faster wireless to devices with older G or 2.4ghz N (provided they have an ethernet port).

It's not for everyone, and I'm still biased towards ethernet if possible, coax if possible, powerline if possible, and then this in descending order. Since powerline and coax can be finicky, this may be your best bet (with a AC router).
title: A few glitches. but solid nonetheless

I love the Sennheiser brand and have owned other products of theirs that have been fantastic. It's a shame that these otherwise wonderful earbuds are compromised by the shoddy poorly-designed case. review_text:
I hate to add my name to the growing list of users that are experiencing the drastic drop in download speed, essentially overnight. My router has worked fine with no problems for about 6 months., until this morning, when the download speed went to a crawl from 30 Meg to less that 0.5 meg. Switching out to my older WNDR 3400 I had left set up completely eliminated the problem. Unbelievable. Having isolated the problem to the router, I switched back to it and updated the firmware. No change. The only item that seemed to help was completely eliminating QOS or WWM settings from on to off. Pretty much got back my speed, but it takes several seconds for the full speed to be reached watching a speed test run, where in the past it jumped to above the rated internet speed instantly and then dropped to my normal max paid for speed. It does not seem that this problem affects upload speed, but only download. I still get my rated 5 Meg uploads. Really an unusual problem, as I did NOTHING to cause this problem to occur, and initially figured it was a provider problem. But the easy swap out of my WNDR 3400 router made the tracking down of the source the problem. I tried resetting my internet modem, but that did not help. Only all turning off of QOS and WMM services did. Something must have "snapped" in the hardware, as no software or setup of my computers, etc. occurred. The computer and all peripherals stay on all the time. And has been flawless since purchased.

This is my second R7000, and the first/older one still works fine,,,,at another location..but I now don't know for how long. I have a backup WNDR 4500 there, so may be putting it back in service shortly...I hope not....
Anyone else try this work around?

UPDATE: 12-26-2016 Now that I have had a little time to troubleshoot further, it is the QOS function that seems to be causing the problem. Turning it on and off shows the problem comes and goes with it's setting. With the QOS off and the WMM on, the speed seems to start up faster that with WMM off. Hits the highest speed way over my purchased speed, and then drops down to this purchased speed, instead of the other way around. So, if you experience this problem, try first turning both WMM and QOS off, then try using just WMM by itself and see if this corrects the problem. It did for me. BTW, WMM is selected for BOTH internet bands, 2.4 AND 5.0 when I refer to it being on or off.
title: Experienced massive download speed loss overnight.

review_text:
After a very bad experience with a Jensen JTA-230 turntable, I purchased a 1byOne turntable. Unlike the Jensen model (whose USB plug to my computer stopped functioning after two months), my 1byOne model is self-recording to MP3 format and is so easy to use than an old fart like me can do it. (I no longer have to cope with "Audacity" on line, which always caused my blood pressure to rise.) In addition, the speakers are far superior to the tinny sound that came from the Jensen. I have a large record collection, and this is an ideal turntable for my recording purposes.

This is an edited version of the original comment (above). I purchased this turntable mainly due to its ability to convert vinyl records into mp3 sound. Nine weeks after purchasing it, the recording function stopped working. (I tried several different flashdrives to make sure.) So I dropped the five previous stars down to three. It was still under warranty, and 1byone is quickly replacing it (but have your Amazon order number on hand if you call them). I love this little player, but I hope the replacement lasts a bit longer than nine weeks (less than nine weeks actually, since I'm not counting how long it took to ship).

I realize too that a lot of the satisfied customers are rating this turntable on its use solely as a turntable. I have plenty of older, more expensive turntables for that function. I bought this one for its recording function, and if that doesn't work, I can't recommend it.

This is my second edit since I returned the replacement I was sent immediately. I'll be trying one more and then it's three strikes and you're out. I've also dropped my rating down to two stars. Yes, the recording function worked, BUT the replacement I received caused my 33 1/3 records to rub against the rear of the stylus mechanism. This appears to be a major problem for those who gave the turntable one or two stars. (Check it out.)

1byone has good customer service by phone, but Verizon refused to allow me to open its email site. I reported this problem when I phoned 1byone, but they don't appear to have done anything to correct it.

So today I received my second replacement, meaning I've gone through THREE turntables thus far. I returned the first because the recording mechanism stopped recording. In this replacement, the recording ability lasted for a few hours and then died. I had promptly switched from a regular sized 33 1/3 recording due to the fact that this one ALSO rubbed against the stylus mechanism. I was trying to record a 10-inch 33 1/3 record when this replacement died.

I still love the self-recording concept, but I'm afraid the concept doesn't equal the finished product.
title: Self-recording to mp3 format within the turntable itself is a winner... when it works... and then there's the rubbing problem...

Yes, it's the real deal! I'm pretty sure every review here will state that this bundle seemed too good to be true. I was hesitant, just like everyone else, but I noticed it was being distributed by Adorama, which is a name I trust. They have the same bundle on their website and on their eBay store. With regards to the price, something to keep in mind is that the 416 does go on sale a couple of times per year for around $799 and the H6 can be had for $300. But, that's only if you buy them when they happen to be on sale and you're still ahead by $50!

As far as I can tell, these are new units. No scuffs or signs of use at all. However, their packaging wasn't fully sealed (and I don't think ever is), so it makes it a bit harder to tell. I'm trusting that these were brand new. I registered both units with their respective manufacturers and haven't seen anything back from either to indicate there's a problem.

I thought it was pretty funny they put giant stickers on the packaging to make sure it was sold as a kit and not separated. The tightness of that wrapping did cause some damage to the boxes. That was superficial, however, and didn't impact the items inside.

The preamps on the H6 are a bit noisy, which is a known factor with field recorders in this price range. If I keep the gain under a 5 with the 416, it's not bad. Going over 5 does raise the noise floor noticeably. I may look into adding something like a Fethead Phantom to give the mike a boost and reducing the gain on the H6 quite a bit.

I have not really tested the modular microphone attachments as I just needed the H6 unit for recording from the 416.

The 416 sounds amazing, as expected. There are tons of reviews out there in the interwebs that will fill you in on it.
title: Yes it's real, and yes it's worth it.

I received these today after trying a pair of Skullcandy Crushers. I was disappointed in the overall sound quality of the crushers, which was disappointing because I also liked them in so many ways. The haptic bass was definitely nice, but they suffered with music that didn’t have well-defined bass. After tirelessly reading reviews, I decided on these Sony’s. These headphones are amazing in terms of sound quality, have good bass (although I miss the haptic), and well-defines overall. The noise cancellation is sort of shocking, but this is also my first pair of NC headphones. The one thing I am disappointed in is the size of the headphones. They are big and loose on me. I really wish they would make a smaller (or female sized) pair! I haven’t fully decided yet if I will keep them. I hate to part with the sound quality after trying so hard to find something that meets my needs, but they just don’t feel snug. I am debating if I should try to modify them by adding some padding on the top of the headband and trying a replacement pair of ear pads that are thicker, without actually modifying the headphone so as not to void the warranty. It might be worth it. I really think these might have the best sound quality for the price range and for current wireless options. Definitely better than Bose for sound. Plus, the technology with touch sensors, although it has some small downsides, is really great: I couldn’t ask for an easier way to muffle the sound when someone approaches me for conversation! Cupping the right ear is genius!!

In any case, I do recommend these headphones. Sony, please make a smaller size option!!!

OLD REVIEW:

Overall this brand has lost quality over time.

SHORT REVIEW:
-Bluetooth connection spotty
-Adjustable over earpiece is a mess
-Microphone overall terrible, and unusable if any noise is present
-Sound quality and battery life is decent

MORE DETAILED REVIEW:
I had a pair that lasted 3 years, set in place over the earpiece, and good Bluetooth connection (sometimes I would leave the room and return with the connection still intact). The microphone was not great so I would use it mainly inside, but the overall sound quality was decent enough that it made the headphones decent to use. The Bluetooth connection also isn't very great. Sometimes I turn my head with my phone in my pocket and the sound cuts in and out. This happens often, especially when I'm walking on the street. I have to press down more than once sometimes to get it to turn on as well.

I still use the headphones but am seriously looking for a better quality option. If you need quick cheaper headphones this might be good but, but definitely not a long term solution.

review_text:
"YAY - IT'S HERE!", I proclaimed when the man in brown delivered my camera. I tore open the out box and marveled at the beautiful packaging and case that contained this camera and all of it's bits. "Wow,look at all this...", I said. Here is what you get:

1x Camera
1x Dive Housing (waterproof housing)
2x Batteries - the same that most of these cameras take like Apeman, Visiontek, etc. 1050maH and seem to be ok.
1x Battery single port cradle for charging the batteries when outside of the camera.
1x USB chord for the charger and/or camera
1x Instruction booklet
TONS of Mounts and clips - none had 3m tape and were of poor tack
1x Review instruction booklet - wait, what? Instructions of reviews? More on this later...

So I assembled the camera, battery, tripod holder attachment, inserted my SD card (none was included) and powered on the camera - so far, so good. This camera's waterproof housing has a top clasp that simply folds over the edge of the back of the housing and snaps closed. This is different than some cases like, the one Apeman and others use that have a security slider and a double clasp system. The outer lens ring is round and seems to be the same one that many of the cheaper 1080p only action cams use.

As I am going through the menus, I noticed it did not provide a setting for adjusting the angle of view - most of these cams have a way to adjust the 170* angle down to 140*, 110*, 90* etc. Looks like I am stuck with fish-eye on this one - that's ok. I continue with the settings and come to the end of the menu when I realize that there was no setting for anti-shake or Gyro stabilization. Ok, now I am concerned... As I moved on to setting the resolution, I noticed that I am given options for photos with a max resolution of 12M. This is not really a 4k option so I begin to wonder a lot more about what I just bought.

Turns out, this camera is NOT a 4k camera as the chipset will not support this resolution. What it does is shoot 2.7k and interpolates the rest. Basically, this means it just adds more pixels that are close to the pixels next to it through software. This makes for slightly noisy and grainy footage. Dropping the resolution to 2.7k improves this a bit but still introduces a lot of motion blur and tearing in the image. Reducing the resolution yet again to 1080P 60fps brings the camera into a new world with footage that is very good - dare I say on par with gopro. An email about this issue to the seller when un-answered. Speaking about the seller, lets discuss this "Review" instruction booklet.

In the top flap of the case was a small folded color leaflet about leaving a review. Ok, sure, I get it, you want to encourage people to leave reviews about their experience. As I continue to read, there is a mention of a 'free gift" of a 16gb micro SD card if you post a review. It even goes to show pictures of 5 golden starts. It outlines the process of posting a review, taking a picture or screenshot of the review and then emailing it to the company. Then, after what I am sure is a review process of your review, they will send you a memory card.

I am sorry but I will not be bribed for a 5 star review. If the product deserves one, I will give one - however in this case, this product does not. Let this serve as a possible disclaimer to future buyers that these 5 star reviews may have had a possible influence - either subconsciously or otherwise. I deducted stars for the following: 1 star for the weak waterproof housing clasp; 1 star for lack of anti-shake setting, lake of recording angle (lens) setting and, poor audio recording quality; 1 star for the review bribe and lack of email response when I questioned the resolution.

Is this a great camera? No.
Is it a good camera? Sort of... This is a good camera is your don't need more than 1080p recording.

In closing, would I recommend it to a friend? Perhaps to a friend's child as a toy or for online VLOGers who don't need 4k or sound recorded with their videos. It may also be good for filming drone flights.

I hope this review helps!
title: Bribed for my review? Camera is just ok & not 4k

Upon closer examination of the OEM power coed, I observe that it has a blivet on the cord near the 12v plug end that must be the traffic receiver.

This cord has no such receiver and cannot help the 2595LMT receive traffic information.

On the other hand, most of the time traffic information is bogus. And more annoying than useful. The Garmin is constantly binging at me to take an alternate route that never is a better route.

Today I tried following its suggestion to get off the freeway in LA because the Garmin was concerned that the freeway was clogged. It told me to take La Cienega to save 4 minutes. Ha. La Cienega was much, much worse than the freeway and ended up costing me 15 minutes or more. (I think it assumes no one is using surface streets in LA in morning rush hour traffic--a fatal assumption.

Later in the trip it told me the freeway was closed ahead and to take an alternate route. I didn't believe it as I could see with my eyes and the excellent traffic flow in both directions that there was no actual blockage.

So, if you don't mind not having the traffic function, this cord works fine. (And since I don't trust the traffic function, I'll probably turn it off my self -- regardless of cord used.)
